actors.name: 陆青崖 Lu Bluecliff (HO1 The Wanderer)

biography.title: Personal Description 外貌
biography.value: 陆青崖，二十四岁。岘山山阳道人门下的游侠：衣着朴素，腰间一柄佩刀，背上另裹着一柄更好的剑，从不在人前拔出。话少，眼睛不闲着。自幼习武，上墙如走平地，落地无声，出剑快得看不清；人情世故却不是他的本事。认准了的事就会去做——而且他心里压着一件不能对生人说的事。

biography.title: Background 背景
biography.value: Lu Bluecliff 陆青崖 ("blue cliff", after the mountain he grew up on), 24. A wanderer of the jianghu 江湖: plainly dressed, a sabre at his hip and a second, finer sword wrapped on his back that he never draws in front of people. Says little, misses nothing. Trained since childhood by a famous hermit swordsman on Mount Crag 岘山, he can run up a wall, land without a sound and cut faster than you can see (Sword 75, Climb 60, Stealth 60, Dodge 60). What he cannot do is talk his way out of trouble (Credit Rating 20). Play him as a man who has decided what is right and will do it, and who is quietly carrying something he cannot tell strangers.

actors.name: 沈怀珠 Shen Pearl (HO2 The Merchant Heir)

biography.title: Personal Description 外貌
biography.value: 沈怀珠，二十岁。临安大药行的少东家：外袍朴素，内里是绫罗，手上没有茧，随身一只药箱和一方药行印信，天下任何一家分号的掌柜见了都要作揖。聪明，口舌利，习惯用钱解决事情；会看病抓药。家传一门点穴之术，指头按对地方能让人半边身子发麻。不是打手，爱走偏锋。她这辈子头一回体会到什么叫无能为力。

biography.title: Background 背景
biography.value: Shen Pearl 沈怀珠 ("holding a pearl"), 20. Heir to one of the great pharmacy houses of the capital, Lin'an 临安: silk under a plain travelling coat, soft hands, a medicine chest, and a seal that any branch manager in the empire will bow to. Clever, quick-tongued and used to money solving things (Credit Rating 60, Medicine 65, Persuade / Fast Talk / Charm 50–55, Appraise, Accounting). The family also hands down a secret art, Acupoint Strike 点穴: a finger pressed to the right spot numbs an arm or drops a man (base 50). Not a fighter; thinks sideways. Play her as someone who, until this month, had never once been powerless.

description.value: 樊城分号掌柜认得你。The Fencewall branch manager knows you.

actors.name: 谢云骧 Xie Cloudmane (HO3 The Commissioner)

biography.title: Personal Description 外貌
biography.value: 谢云骧，二十二岁。临安高门子弟，朝廷亲封的宣抚使，印绶在身。相貌出众，学问极好，从小就是让人听话的那一个。自幼围猎，一手好弓，是三人里最会射箭的；剑也拿得起来，勉强。他是带着一支军队来的：发小刘卿堂急公好义、一身江湖豪气，听说他督军，主动请缨，替他带着五千兵马一路同来。如今他身上一处伤口不肯收口，也不知道刘卿堂和他的人去了哪里。头一回体会到：没人非得听你的时候，名头值几个钱。

biography.title: Background 背景
biography.value: Xie Cloudmane 谢云骧 ("a horse galloping through clouds"), 22. Youngest son of one of the great families of the capital and now, with the seal to prove it, an imperial Commissioner sent to relieve the twin cities. Handsome, beautifully educated, raised to be obeyed (APP 75, EDU 80, Credit Rating 75, Persuade 65, Law, History). He has hunted since boyhood and is the best archer at the table (Bow 75); he can hold a sword, barely. He arrived with an army, led for him by his childhood friend Captain Liu 刘卿堂, hot-blooded and generous, who volunteered the moment he heard Xie was going to war. Now he has a wound that will not close and no idea what has happened to Liu and his men. Play him as someone finding out, for the first time, what his name is worth when nobody has to obey it.

pages.name: 故事 The story so far

text.content:
The story so far 故事

The year is 1268. The Song 宋 empire is old and rich and dying, and the Mongols 蒙古 under Kublai Khan 忽必烈 have come south to finish it. In the middle of China two walled cities face each other across the Han River 汉江: Fencewall 樊城 on the north bank and Southbright 襄阳 on the south. Whoever holds them holds the road to the Yangtze and to the capital, Lin'an 临安. A floating bridge used to join them.

Two weeks ago, after a three-day assault, Fencewall fell. Its commander, Commander Fan 范天顺, hanged himself rather than surrender; his nephew, Magistrate Fan 范玉楼, opened the gates to spare the forty thousand people inside. The famous archer of the garrison, Niu 牛富, refused to surrender and sits in the gaol. The Mongol commander, Marshal Ashu 阿术, keeps his army on a tight leash: no looting, no burning. But patrols walk every street, the bridge has been cut, and soldiers watch the riverbank day and night. Across the water Southbright still holds. In a few days the Mongols mean to cross and take it.

Then a fog came down on the river. In January, when the Han never makes fog. Boats go out and do not come back. Townsfolk say they dream of the Lady of the Han 汉江神女 calling them to the water.

Everyone in this town who matters wants the same thing: to get across that river. You are three such people, strangers to one another, who will meet tonight in the reeds east of the city, where a one-armed boatman has promised, for a price, to row passengers over in the dark.

A wandering swordsman 游侠 who walked into the marshal's victory feast ten nights ago, tried to kill him, cut only his shoulder, and is now the most hunted man in Fencewall.

A merchant's heir 商贾 from the capital's great pharmacy house, who watched her father beheaded on the road outside the gate and must get home to a house with no head.

A commissioner of the court 命官, sent with an army to save these cities, whose last eight hundred men crossed the river without him and have not been heard from since.

This is a wuxia 武侠 story, not a horror story: it is about people, loyalty and debts, swords and the river. Think of the classic Jin Yong 金庸 novels, or films like Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon. But something is in the water tonight that is older than the war, and the fog is not weather.

Tonight (Session 0) 今夜

Each of you first plays a short scene of your own: how you came to be in Fencewall and why you must leave. Then the three of you meet at the riverbank for the night crossing. The session ends when you reach shelter on the north bank, in the coffin shop 棺材铺 of a woman called Winding Stream 曲流.

Who's who 人物

What people in Fencewall would tell you about each other. Names are given English-first, with the Chinese after.

The three of you 你们

Lu Bluecliff 陆青崖
HO1 The Wanderer 游侠
24. A wandering swordsman from Mount Crag 岘山; plain clothes, a sabre at his hip and a wrapped sword on his back he never shows. Says little, misses nothing.
Shen Pearl 沈怀珠
HO2 The Merchant Heir 商贾
20. Heir to a great pharmacy house of the capital 临安; silk under a plain coat, soft hands, a medicine chest. Clever, quick-tongued, used to money solving things.
Xie Cloudmane 谢云骧
HO3 The Commissioner 命官
22. Youngest son of a great family and the court's Commissioner, seal and all. Handsome, educated, raised to be obeyed; the best archer at the table; carries a wound that will not close.

The Mongols 蒙古

Marshal Ashu 阿术
Mongol commander-in-chief
Of the Uriankhai; Kublai 忽必烈's right arm. A brilliant general and a terrifying fighter: well over six feet, bearded, a huge sabre. Took Fencewall in three days; forbids looting. Wounded in the shoulder at his own victory feast.
Duan Driftwood 段游衍
Song general turned Mongol
From the Dali 大理 clan. Surrendered to the Song, then to the Mongols; sits one seat down from Ashu and does his talking in Chinese. Smooth, pleasant, and the man every scholar loves to curse.
General Toghan 脱欢
Mongol general
One of Ashu's generals. Barely speaks Chinese; hard and greedy. Commands the detachments on the roads around the city.
Mongol soldiers 蒙古兵
Patrols and guards
Foot and horse. Everywhere in town after dark; they carry weapons, tokens, money and written orders.

The Song 宋

Commander Fan 范天顺
Late commander of Fencewall
Beloved, hard-working, harsh with wrongdoers. Refused to surrender and hanged himself in the Magistracy 衙署 on the night of 3 January.
Magistrate Fan 范玉楼
Fan's nephew; runs the town for the Mongols
Opened the gates the morning after his uncle's death to spare the people. Now flatters Ashu at banquets. Embarrassing to watch; perhaps not a coward.
Niu the Archer 牛富
Garrison commander, in the gaol
Forties, dark, lean as a bowstring, eyes like torches. His God-Arm Bow 神臂弓 shoots four hundred paces; before the siege he shot Ashu's nephew dead. Refused to surrender; the Mongols cut his hand-tendons and locked him up.
Prefect Xu 许德显
The region's prefect
A senior Song official who stayed on and now dines at Ashu's table. His family owns boats.
Captain Liu 刘卿堂
HO3's oldest friend
Hot-blooded, generous, a jianghu 江湖 air about him. Led HO3's last eight hundred men across the river on 3 January. Not seen since.

People of Fencewall 樊城人

Winding Stream 曲流
Owner of the coffin shop 棺材铺 by the river
About fifty, tall and heavily built, an ex-caravan guard with a big blade on her back. Gentle with guests; makes the best coffins in town. Your shelter after the crossing.
Boatman Wang 船夫王
The one-armed boatman
Curses the Mongols and the court in the same breath. For a price he will row you across tonight.
The Jiang twins 姜楼、姜阁
Fishermen brothers
Strong swimmers who know every reed-bed. Jiang Tower is the steady elder, Jiang Loft the reckless younger.
Doctor Yue 越南柯
A wandering healer
Handsome, charming, hands like a conjurer's; turns up where he is least expected and gives money to the poor.
Autumn 秋筠
A scar-faced woman outlaw
Town gossip: hides somewhere in the back streets, hunted by both sides.
The drowned 溺者
What the fog brings
Boats go out and do not come back. Some townsfolk are found at the bank at dawn, soaked, remembering nothing.

Opening narrative 开场

Read aloud by the GM, lights low, title screen on, before the three personal intros. Then each player gives a name and one visible detail.

Listen.

There is a river in the middle of China called the Han 汉江. In winter it runs grey and wide and slow, and for a thousand years it has been the line between north and south. On its two banks stand two walled cities, close enough that on a clear day a man on one wall can watch the sentries pace on the other: Fencewall 樊城 to the north, Southbright 襄阳 to the south. Between them, until last week, there was a bridge.

The year is 1268. The empire of the Song 宋 is old and gold and soft, and it has forgotten how to fight. Out of the north have come the Mongols 蒙古, who have never forgotten. They have broken kingdoms from the Yellow Sea to the gates of Europe, and now their horses stand on the north bank of the Han, and their marshal, a man called Ashu 阿术 of the Uriankhai, has taken Fencewall in three days. The commander of the garrison hanged himself. The magistrate opened the gates. The bridge is gone. Across the water Southbright still holds, its watch-fires small and stubborn in the dark, and everyone in Fencewall who has somewhere else to be is looking at those fires and wondering how to reach them.

This is not a world of monsters. This is a world of people: of soldiers and merchants and officials, and of another kind of people who live in the cracks between them, in what is called the jianghu 江湖, the rivers and lakes. Wanderers. Swordsmen who owe nothing to the emperor and everything to their masters. People who can run up a wall and down the other side, who can put a finger on your neck and stop your arm, who carry old grudges and older swords. If you have seen a film where two fighters duel on the roof of a teahouse, you know them.

Three of those people are in Fencewall tonight.

One of you is a wanderer 游侠, young and fast and poor, with a sword that does not belong to you and a thing you did ten nights ago that the whole city is whispering about.

One of you is the heir to a great house of medicine 商贾, from the capital 临安 far to the south, who came north with a convoy and a father and will go home with neither.

One of you is a commissioner of the court 命官, born to one of the oldest families in the empire, sent here with five thousand men to save a city that has already fallen, and still carrying the wound that kept you from leaving with the rest.

None of you has met the others. Each of you has a reason to cross the river. Each of you has a secret you would rather keep.

It is the eleventh of January. There is no moon. The guards on the bank change at midnight, and for a few minutes nobody is watching the reeds east of the city, where a one-armed boatman has promised, for a price, to take passengers across.

And it is foggy. In midwinter. Over a river that has never, in anyone's memory, made fog in January.

Let's meet you.

Player Primer: the Han River, 1268 玩家入门：一二六八年的汉江

This is a wuxia story set at a real moment in history. You are not superheroes; you are ordinary people in a collapsing world who happen to have skills.

The situation 时局

It is the last years of the Southern Song 宋 dynasty. The court is corrupt, the emperor is busy chasing immortality, and Chancellor Jia 贾似道 runs the government. In the north, Kublai Khan 忽必烈's Mongol cavalry wins every battle.

Two cities face each other across the Han River: Fencewall 樊城 on the north bank and Southbright 襄阳 on the south. They are the gate to the whole south. Southbright is ringed by water and nearly impregnable; Fencewall is not. A pontoon bridge once joined them; the Mongols 蒙古 cut it.

On 3 January 1268 the Mongols stormed Fencewall. Commander Fan 范天顺 hanged himself rather than surrender; his nephew, Magistrate Fan 范玉楼, opened the gates. Marshal Ashu 阿术 forbade looting, so life goes on, except for the patrols on every street. In six days the army crosses to attack Southbright.

And now an unnatural fog has settled on the river. Townsfolk dream of the Lady of the Han 汉江神女; old tales of Red Pine the Rain Master 雨师赤松子 are told again.

Who you are 你们是谁

Three pre-built characters, three different ways of living. Pick one; names and details are yours to change.

Lu Bluecliff 陆青崖 ("blue cliff", after the mountain he grew up on), 24. What he cannot do is talk his way out of trouble (Credit Rating 20). Play him as a man who has decided what is right and will do it, and who is quietly carrying something he cannot tell strangers.

HO2 The Merchant Heir HO2 商贾

Shen Pearl 沈怀珠 ("holding a pearl"), 20. Heir to one of the great pharmacy houses of the capital, Lin'an 临安: silk under a plain travelling coat, soft hands, a medicine chest, and a seal that any branch manager in the empire will bow to. Clever, quick-tongued and used to money solving things (Credit Rating 60, Medicine 65, Persuade / Fast Talk / Charm 50–55, Appraise, Accounting). The family also hands down a secret art, Acupoint Strike 点穴: a finger pressed to the right spot numbs an arm or drops a man (base 50). Not a fighter; thinks sideways. Play her as someone who, until this month, had never once been powerless.

HO3 The Commissioner HO3 命官

Xie Cloudmane 谢云骧 ("a horse galloping through clouds"), 22. Youngest son of one of the great families of the capital and now, with the seal to prove it, an imperial Commissioner sent to relieve the twin cities. Handsome, beautifully educated, raised to be obeyed (APP 75, EDU 80, Credit Rating 75, Persuade 65, Law, History). He has hunted since boyhood and is the best archer at the table (Bow 75); he can hold a sword, barely. He arrived with an army, led for him by his childhood friend Captain Liu 刘卿堂, hot-blooded and generous, who volunteered the moment he heard Xie was going to war. Now he has a wound that will not close and no idea what has happened to Liu and his men. Play him as someone finding out, for the first time, what his name is worth when nobody has to obey it.

Each of you has a reason you must leave Fencewall, and a secret you keep from the others. You must cross the Han River under the Mongols' noses.

What the jianghu is 什么是江湖

The jianghu is the world the government cannot reach: sects, wanderers, caravan guards, bandits, quack doctors, storytellers. A wanderer lives by yi, righteousness: help the wronged, repay kindness, repay insult. Lightness 轻功 skill lets you leap walls; inner power and acupoint strikes are the stuff of legend. Think Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon; Hero; Kung Fu Hustle.

A note on history 历史提示

The scenario bends history (the real siege lasted until 1273). You can change what happens to people here; you cannot change how the war ends.

Rules Cheat Sheet 规则速查

The one rule 一个核心规则

Roll d100. Equal to or under your skill = success. Under half = Hard success; under a fifth = Extreme. 01 is a critical; 100 (or 96–100 if the skill is below 50) is a fumble.

  • Bonus / penalty die: roll an extra tens die, keep the better / worse.
  • Push: after a failure, describe a riskier attempt and reroll once; fail again and something bad happens.
  • Opposed roll: both roll, higher success level wins.
  • Luck: spend Luck points one-for-one to turn a failed roll into a success.

Combat 战斗

  • Act in DEX order, one action a round.
  • When attacked, Dodge or Fight Back; compare success levels.
  • Major wound: lose half your max HP in one hit → CON roll or pass out. 0 HP with a major wound → dying.
  • Armour subtracts from damage. Mongol soldiers have 2.

This scenario's wuxia rules 本模组的武侠规则

  • Lightness 轻功 = Climb and Jump. Scaling walls, roofs and leaps use these two skills.
  • Acupoint Strike 点穴: a custom skill anyone may use (HO2 base 50, others base 10). The author's rules attachment is missing; until we have it, use this house rule: Acupoint Strike opposed by the target's CON; success paralyses the target for 1D3 rounds or lets this attack ignore armour. Against the Undying Servants 不死仆从 a hit on the injection scar on the spine kills outright (as in the finale). The Ling family needles give +10%.
  • Caps (author's reference): attributes 80 max / 30 min; skills 75 max / 55 for the second tier. HO bonuses may exceed them.
  • Don't go low on POW: the thing in the river tries its Dream-Call 梦引 every night, an opposed POW roll.
  • Action rounds: once the sandbox starts, three free-action rounds a day (morning, noon, evening). Meals, the Wineshop and Autumn 秋筠's help do not cost a round.
  • Sanity: roll SAN when you see something wrong; "0/1" means lose 0 on a pass, 1 on a fail.

Time and distance 时间与距离

  • The river between the two cities is about 1.5 km wide. Tonight you can see about 10 m.
  • One pace ≈ 1.5 m; four hundred paces ≈ 600 m.

journal.name: HO1 游侠 · The Wanderer（仅HO1玩家）

text.content:
HO1 The Wanderer
HO1 游侠 · 弓背霞明剑，霜寒照吴钩

Who you are 你是谁

You are Lu Bluecliff 陆青崖, twenty-four, a wandering swordsman raised on Mount Crag 岘山 by the Hermit 山阳道人, the only father you have known. Ten nights ago, at the Mongols 蒙古' victory feast in the Magistracy 衙署, you tried to kill Marshal Ashu 阿术 with your master's poisoned sword Stillwater 止水 and only cut his shoulder. An old classmate, Duan Driftwood 段游衍, now serving the Mongols, covered your escape. The whole city is hunting you. You need to be across the river tonight, and you still owe your master a head.

Public 公开信息

You are the disciple of the Hermit of Mount Crag, and you are very good at what you do. For players who love classic wuxia and act on their heart. Any one combat skill +20.

Your secret (for your eyes only) 你的秘密（仅本人阅读）

Your master is the Hermit of Mount Crag (his real name is Chen Yangshan 陈阳山). People say he inherited the arts of Red Pine the Rain Master 雨师赤松子 and can walk through fire and ride the wind. Most of that is talk, but he did make you a true wanderer.

You had a classmate, Duan Driftwood, from the Dali 大理 clan, who studied under your master for a year and left. Your master praised his quick mind and wide learning, but told you not to grow close to him.

When Fencewall 樊城 fell, your master gave you his famous sword, Stillwater, and told you to do as the assassins of old did: kill the Mongol marshal, Ashu. The blade is coated with a rare poison, Rainmaster's Ink 雨师墨. He warned you three times not to use it lightly.

On 10 January the Mongols held a victory banquet at the Magistracy. You got in. But Ashu is a formidable fighter and well guarded; you only cut his shoulder. At the banquet you saw Duan Driftwood, now serving the Mongols. He covered your escape, and you have been hiding in Fencewall since.

The Mongols are hunting you. You must leave Fencewall, soon.

Character requirements 车卡要求

  • You carry the sword Stillwater. It is your master's weapon; your own weapon is up to you.
  • Trained since childhood: DEX +10, STR +10, one combat skill +20, Climb or Jump +15.
  • These bonuses are already on your pre-built sheet.

journal.name: HO2 商贾 · The Merchant Heir（仅HO2玩家）

text.content:
HO2 The Merchant Heir
HO2 商贾 · 市井怀珠玉，往来人未逢

Who you are 你是谁

You are Shen Pearl 沈怀珠, twenty, heir to a great pharmacy house in the capital, Lin'an 临安. Two weeks ago, on the road outside the North Gate 北门, Mongol riders stopped your father's medicine convoy and beheaded him in front of you; you ran into the city alone. Then the city fell. Your foster brother Yue Nanke 越南柯 is somewhere out in the jianghu 江湖, and the house at home has no head. You need to get across the river and go home.

Public 公开信息

You are the heir of a famous pharmacy house from the capital, and very rich. For players who think sideways. Custom skill: Acupoint Strike 点穴, base 50.

Your secret (for your eyes only) 你的秘密（仅本人阅读）

Your family's pharmacy house in the capital is famous. You decide its name, its reputation and how it does business: in bed with officials, grasping and heartless, or charitable. It has branches across the empire since the 1040s, and some branch managers are crooks.

You have a foster brother, Yue Nanke 越南柯, the son of your father's old friend, raised with you. A few years ago he vanished into the jianghu without a word; since then, only letters.

In the last month of 1267 you and your father escorted a convoy of medicine for the army. Outside Fencewall 樊城 the Mongols 蒙古 stopped you. Your father was killed in front of you; you fled alone into the city.

With your father dead the house has no head. You must get home, which means leaving Fencewall.

Character requirements 车卡要求

  • Credit Rating +10. Name the pharmacy house and decide its ethos; it determines how townsfolk treat you.
  • Medicine +30. The Fencewall branch manager knows you.
  • Family art: custom skill Acupoint Strike, base 50.
  • These bonuses are already on your pre-built sheet.

journal.name: HO3 命官 · The Commissioner（仅HO3玩家）

text.content:
HO3 The Commissioner
HO3 命官 · 翻弓骋猿臂，承箭惜貂裘

Who you are 你是谁

You are Xie Cloudmane 谢云骧, twenty-two, youngest son of a great family of the capital 临安 and, seal and all, the court's Commissioner sent to save the twin cities. The Mongols 蒙古 destroyed your army on the road; you reached Fencewall 樊城 with eight hundred men. On 3 January your oldest friend Captain Liu 刘卿堂 led them across the river to Southbright 襄阳 while you, wounded, stayed behind; the next morning the city surrendered. You have heard nothing from Liu since. You need to get across the river and find your men.

Public 公开信息

You are a Commissioner appointed by the court itself, seal and all. For players who like talking their way through. Bow +30.

Your secret (for your eyes only) 你的秘密（仅本人阅读）

You come from one of the great families of the capital. Life has been easy; you hold a comfortable sinecure. In 1267, for reasons you decide (a rival's scheme, or your own idealism), you were made Commissioner and sent to relieve the siege of the twin cities.

Your childhood friend Liu Qingtang 刘卿堂, hot-blooded and generous, volunteered to come with you and led your five thousand men.

The Mongols cut you to pieces. By the end of 1267 you broke through into Fencewall with eight hundred men left. In January the assault began and Commander Fan 范天顺 ordered you across to Southbright. You were still carrying a wound from the breakout (you decide what) and could not travel. On 3 January Liu took the eight hundred across the river. The next day Magistrate Fan 范玉楼 surrendered the city.

Everything north of the river is Mongol now. You must cross to Southbright and rejoin your men.

Character requirements 车卡要求

  • A noble's upbringing and a hunter's eye: Bow +30.
  • APP +10; EDU +10 and never below 70.
  • A civil post; whether you have seen battle before is up to you.
  • These bonuses are already on your pre-built sheet.

journal.name: 规则卡与文书 · Rules cards & handouts

text.content:
Set-piece rules 规则卡

The book shows these two cards to the players before the scene.

The rescue of Niu the Archer (15 January, noon) 劫法场

  • You command every friendly wanderer except Nameless Fang; the GM rolls for them.
  • Your side acts, then the soldiers. No DEX order. Soldiers go for whoever is nearest the carts.
  • Five rounds, then Mongol reinforcements arrive. Leave with Niu = win.
  • Stop the road: topple a painted gate-tower, or kill the cart horses.
  • Anyone up in a gallery can shoot at any target with any ranged skill; a miss may hit a friend or a bystander.
  • Closing with a horseman or a cart horse: DEX (or Dodge) and your fighting skill together; fail and a hoof does 2+1D3.
  • One round to reach a cart; one round and STR or Locksmith to open it. Three shackled prisoners per cart; one person carries one prisoner. Only Fang knows Niu's face.
  • Leaving: ranged fighters get away free; melee fighters roll DEX, and if they fail a wanderer covers them and dies. On a horse: bonus die. Carrying a prisoner: penalty die.

The Watchtower (the last night) 塔楼

  • The Wanderer goes out on the river with the boatman to draw the thing up, and shows the bank where it is with fire. Bring a boat, a boatman and a way to make light. Each round: signal, or attack the spine. Gunpowder may be too damp (Luck).
  • The Merchant Heir holds the foot of the tower against the Undying; other wanderers may help; Doctor Yue will not be there. She acts first each round: DEX — fail / success / Extreme / critical = 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 actions; each action is an Acupoint Strike (+10% with the Ling needles) that kills one of them outright.
  • The Commissioner shoots from the top of the tower with a bow that can reach mid-river, only in a round the Wanderer signals. Captain Liu watches the water: if he spots it, bonus die.
  • The tower is 50 m of timber: CON to climb. Two guards below, one above.

Handouts 文书与残页

Show a section to the players when they find it (right-click the heading in the page list → Show to Players, or read aloud).

Prefect Xu's two letters (from Doctor Yue) 许德显的两封信

To the Mongol camp: "…your servant Xu, prefect of this circuit, has long admired the Great Khan's virtue and the Marshal's might… the city cannot stand; I beg to be of use when the gates open. My household keeps three painted barges and five skiffs, which I offer with both hands…"
To Governor Lü Wenhuan at Southbright: "…every word written in blood… my loyalty to the Song could be cut open and shown to the sun and moon… if the city falls I will die with it, and ask only that Your Excellency remember a faithful servant…"

The Hermit's letter (Duan's room) 陈阳山的信

"You urged me more than once to leave Mount Crag. I know the times are bad and that going is best, but I am old and cannot bear the road, and my pupil is in a den of wolves — how could I leave alone? If HO1 succeeds, the name will be known under heaven and written in the histories; if not, I beg you, for the sake of old days, to save a life. I enclose what remains of Red Pine as payment. The cliff is high and the road long; take care of yourself." — Chen Yangshan 陈阳山

Toghan's note (Duan's room) 脱欢的短讯

"The Marshal feasts the three armies at the Magistracy; fed and watered, we take the city the day after. Wang Wu's restaurant in Fencewall will feed the men left on the warships: ten oxen, eight sheep, thirty fowl each, fifteen jars of old wine, delivered by the restaurant's own people on the evening of the 17th. The men on the ships are few; stay alert; let no rogue slip in among them. General Duan will see to it."

The defence map (Duan's room) 樊城襄阳布防图

Both banks, garrisons and places of note. The tower on the Fencewall bank is marked separately, with a note in small characters: "Fine view: boats in the river and the movements of the Southbright garrison all in sight."

Two old recipes (the pharmacy) 两张古方

牵机药 Bowstring: from ripe strychnine seeds; very bitter, a peculiar scent. After a quarter hour the muscles tighten and the mind grows anxious; after half an hour the back arches until head meets heels and the face is locked in a grin; fully conscious throughout; death by suffocation in about an hour.
十香软经散 Ten-Scent Powder: ten spices with datura and 软骨草; a white powder without colour or smell. Instant: the whole body goes slack and cannot move; after some days the martial skill is gone for good.

Green Rot (Autumn's room) 绿腐

"…chant the sutra, and give the cursed one a fresh green leaf. For seven days the organs rot within, until what is left is a heap of green mould. There is one release only: the death of the one who cast it."

The traveller's record (Fan's study) 游记

"Beside Mount Qiao, in the waters of the Qiao, lives a great fish called He Luo 何罗: one head and ten bodies, like hundreds of fish twined together, turning and turning without rest. I had thought it lived only in the Qiao; but when I was banished to Tanzhou, people near Lake Dongting had seen it. They told me that whenever He Luo appears a great fog rises over the lake, and no boat can pass."

The poem on the desk (Fan's study) 案头的诗

Dawn on the Jingzhou road, night on the dyke of Lake Tai. / The lake ten thousand acres; waves rolling a thousand years. / Cold moon, heavy frost; a crow cries, breaking sleep. / I walk in moonlight to find the tide and lightly leave the world. / Riding cloud and coloured mist, bending light to blue smoke, / the goddess lays a hand on my head; her attendants laugh. / Silk of every colour; wine poured for a feast. / Lucky to see this; joy at its height. / A cold wind rises; I wake as from lightning, / a lifetime away, standing by Lake Tai, / and hear a voice calling me, calling, so sad. / I dare not stay, and write this of the night.

The torn pages (Fan's coffin) 棺中残页

"Who eats the flesh of the He Luo fish has his marrow washed and his sinews changed, his spine drawn out; a web of fine lines grows on his back. He needs no grain, but cannot bear the sun, and hides by day to walk at night. All who eat it learn the art called Green Rot… To end the art, end the man; there is no other way…"
"The He Luo fish shuns light and heat and fears fire more than tigers; so do those who have eaten it, the one like lips to the other's teeth… It lies on the river-bed and does not rise unless a boat passes over…"

From the book stall 书摊

The Lost Pendant 遗佩情事: Zheng Jiaofu 郑交甫 of Jin met the two jewelled daughters of the Han on its bank, lost his heart, and begged their pendants with a poem. When the goddesses had gone the pendants vanished from his hands. "The spirit-consort, lovely and free, seen at times on the river's brink; fine robes, light steps, a glance that gives grace. Jiaofu met her and spoke his private heart; the ringing pendant thrown away, her shadow gone past following."
The Rain Master 雨师记: Red Pine 赤松子, first of the ten immortals of old, Rain Master to the Divine Farmer; he walked into fire unburnt and rose and fell with wind and rain… One day he played chess in the mountains with his elder brother Red Beard; a woodcutter set down his axe to watch. Red Pine had him hold a date-stone in his mouth, and his hunger and thirst were gone. When the game ended and the woodcutter stooped for his load, the axe-handle had rotted away.

From the Library 藏书阁

A physician's notes on Rainmaster's Ink: the wound festers and gives off a sick damp stench; the pulse clogs; the blood runs backward. Deep poisoning festers over the whole body; shallow poisoning festers for months or a year, then re-opens in every spell of rain.
The Lady of the Han, another version: Zheng Jiaofu met the goddess of the Han, liked her looks, spoke rudely, and asked her pendant as a betrothal gift. She hid her anger and untied it, and named a midnight meeting. He went and found no beauty: a starving wolf five feet long stood in the way and ate him whole, leaving only the pendant on the bank, which it could not chew. The place is called the Lost Pendant Shoal.
Annotated Records of the Three Kingdoms: Guan Yu attacked Fencewall when the Han flooded, drowned the seven armies and shook the empire; then Sun Quan broke faith, Lü Meng took Jiangling, Guan Yu's men scattered, and he was taken and killed at Linju.

The three temptations (the reeds) 三惑迷津

The River Lord: "I am He Bo 冯夷, and I fish here for all the world. I waited five hundred years for the first fish and three hundred for the second. When the fish bites, white waves stand like mountains and the sea shakes with a sound like gods and ghosts, dread for a thousand miles. I give the fish to the people of both banks and they are not hungry for a year… Good, good. The dust of the world is all entanglement; better to be an idle guest. Friends, will you fish here with me? One fish is a hundred years; one feeds both banks."
The goddess: "I was a maid of Eastern Ou given to King Zhao of Zhou, and sailed the river with him. The men of Chu plotted; the boat sank mid-river, the king drowned, and I and my sisters followed him into the water. The world calls us loyal and chaste — but do you know what lies on the bed of the Han? Ghosts, and horned dragons, waiting to gnaw my flesh. That is the price of loyalty… The Song's number is up; how long will the Yuan last? Drift with me on the river, free."
The Many-Headed Fish: a fish with one head and ten bodies rises from the boiling river, crying like a bird, clear and long; the ten bodies swim ten ways and the whole Han shakes — the very He Luo of the Classic of Mountains and Seas.

pages.name: 沙盒 How the sandbox runs

text.content:
GM: how the sandbox runs 主持人：自由调查轮

After the ginger "candy" at the coffin shop, the town map comes out and the game becomes a semi-sandbox: 12–15 January (four days), the warship raid on the 16th/17th, the Mongol crossing planned for the 18th. The book estimates about 40 hours in total. Keep the three threads in view: the gaol (Niu 牛富 and his bow), the boats (Prefect Xu 许德显, the fishermen, the Mongol warships) and the thing in the river (Fan's rite, the Undying, the Watchtower 塔楼).

Action rounds 行动轮

  • Each day has three rounds: morning, noon, evening. One round = the party (together or split) goes to one place and does one thing there. Nights are for fixed events and dreams.
  • Free (no round): eating at the restaurant or coffin shop, the hidden wineshop 酒肆 once they know it, Autumn's 秋筠 disguise help once a day, chance meetings on the street (optional events), and anything the book marks "does not cost a round".
  • The Street Crossing 街口 joins Front Street and Back Street; moving between them passes through it (noon on the 12th and 15th it has fixed events).
  • Mongol patrols are everywhere. HO1 is on the wanted posters (Duan blurred the likeness: describe only an outline). Whenever HO1 is out undisguised: Disguise 乔装, or the party's lowest Luck; on a failure HO1 rolls DEX to shake the soldiers and loses that round's destination.
  • Making a poison at the pharmacy (牵机药 / 十香软经散) is one Hard Medicine roll a day.
  • Rolls in this scenario are never pushed inside set pieces (rescue, assassination, raid, finale).

The four districts 四区

DistrictPlacesWho you meet
Front Street 前街street stalls & old-book seller · Li Family Theatre 李家瓦子 · Wang Wu's Restaurant 王五分茶 · the pharmacy (HO2's house) · the Teahouse 茶楼 · the Coffin Shop 棺材铺 · the Undying family's house · the hidden Wineshop 酒肆Doctor Yue, Autumn, Wang Wu, Chen the flag-bearer, Toghan at noon, Ling Xuchun, tea master Song, Du, the monk, Nameless Fang
Back Street 后街the Guildhall 会馆 (Mongol billet, Duan's room) · the burning house · Seven Treasures 七宝行 jewellerDuan, Toghan's staff, the jeweller
Street Crossing 街口inns, tea stalls, the execution groundcrowds; the Hermit's body (12th); Niu's cage carts (15th)
Magistracy quarter 衙署Fan's residence & mourning hall · Prefect Xu's mansion · Niu's house (now Ashu's quarters) · the School & Library 官学/藏书阁 · the Gaol 监牢Magistrate Fan, Xu, Ashu, the scholars, prisoners
Riverbank 汉江沿岸East dock: fishermen's huts, the Mongol warships · West dock: the ruined Pavilion 解佩亭 · the Watchtower 塔楼 · the reeds · the Temple 寺庙 by the wallfishermen, Ling Daiqiu, dreamers at night, the Undying

Fixed events, day by day 固定事件

WhenEventPage
11 Jan nightHO3's first Dream-Call (POW; SAN 1/1D3).Optional & personal
12 Jan noonStreet Crossing: the Hermit of Mount Crag 山阳道人 hangs on a spear. SAN 1/1D3 for HO1.Street Crossing
12 JanWang Wu's Restaurant is shut (the watchman's brawl). The pharmacy: Ling Xuchun 凌序春 comes for medicine on the party's first visit.Front Street
12 Jan eveningDoctor Yue 越南柯 at the coffin shop with Xu's letters.Front Street
12 Jan nightHO3's second Dream-Call: the riverbank, the spine, Captain Liu 刘卿堂 joins.Optional & personal
From 13 JanLiu travels with HO3. The night events can fire: the Temple ambush (after Chen's invitation), the Undying house raid, the Rashomon alley meeting.Temple / Front Street / Optional
15 Jan noonNiu the Archer is brought to the Street Crossing to be beheaded: the rescue.Street Crossing
16 JanIf Niu was rescued: he hands over the God-Arm Bow 神臂弓 through Nameless Fang 方未名.Street Crossing
17 Jan eveningAshu's banquet for the army before the crossing; the warships are lightly held: the raid "沉舟绝渡".Riverbank
Any day after the planThe assassination at Ashu's sickroom → the city locks down → the Watchtower finale that night.Magistracy quarter / Finale
18 JanPlanned Mongol river assault on Southbright (never happens if Gla'aki is still in the river).—

What the finale needs 决战前置

  • A boat and a boatman who will row into the fog: Wang Wu's or the theatre's 乌篷船 boat; the fishermen (only if Ling Daiqiu 凌代秋 is cured) or the Jiang twins; or Prefect Xu's painted barges.
  • A light signal from the boat: gunpowder from Xu or Magistrate Fan (Luck roll in the wet fog), or the Fire-Cloak spell from the Hermit's pages.
  • A bow that reaches mid-river: only Niu's God-Arm Bow (400 paces). Mongol bows reach 300.
  • The Ling needles 凌家绣花针 for HO2's Acupoint Strike (+10%): recovered by killing Autumn.
  • Knowing the weakness: a thin point driven into the healed wound on the spine kills an Undying outright (the Undying house, the torn pages, the physician's notes).

The clue web 线索网

  • Doctor Yue → Xu's two letters → Xu's boats, gunpowder, gaol access.
  • The Teahouse → tea master Song → the Wineshop address → Du, the monk, Nameless Fang → the rescue plan.
  • The pharmacy → Ling Xuchun → Ling Daiqiu's poisoning → Autumn at the Li Theatre → the needles; the Library → Rainmaster's Ink vs the green mould (two different things).
  • The Gaol or the burning house → the Undying family's house → the spine weakness → Nameless Fang on the wall.
  • The Wang Wu restaurant → Chen 陈寻忠 → the Temple ambush → Liu's truth; Wang Wu himself → Fan's plan → the warship raid.
  • Fan's study and coffin → the Many-Headed Fish 何罗鱼 and the pages → Magistrate Fan's assassination request.
  • Seven Treasures jeweller → the Grand Lake Stone 太湖石 → the Pavilion ruins.
  • Duan's room → Toghan's note (the banquet date) and the defence map (the Watchtower's view) → the raid and the finale.

Front Street 前街

The commercial street, at a third of its old bustle. Mongol patrols pass constantly. Wanted posters for HO1 on the walls (blurred).

The street stalls and the old-book seller 沿街浮屋 · 旧书摊

Stalls against the house-fronts: snacks, curios, household goods; worth a rummage. The book stall is run by Wang Jianchuan 王见川: thirty, heavy-browed, full-faced, built like a porter but dressed as a scholar (square cap, washed-out robe, feather fan), a voice like a bell. Magistrate Fan 范玉楼 and the school's scholars sometimes browse here and will talk (see Optional: "A chance meeting over books").

On the stall: popular novels, poetry, local tales of the strange. Two are useful (handouts "The Lost Pendant" and "The Rain Master"): the romance of Zheng Jiaofu 郑交甫 and the goddess of the Han, and the legend of Red Pine the Rain Master 赤松子 (the woodcutter whose axe-handle rotted while he watched one game of chess).

The Li Family Theatre 李家瓦子

Fencewall's famous pleasure-house, now dead: a tall painted gate-tower outside, a square courtyard, the red doors hacked by axes and hooves. In the dry pool of the courtyard lies a stranded black-awning boat 乌篷船. Two-storey galleries, dusty hangings, an empty stage.

Mistress Wang 王氏, fifty-odd, the owner, invites the party in for tea. Husband and son taken for corvée labour; only she and her five-year-old daughter remain, "and a homeless young woman we took in". The performers fled; the men were pressed, the women went to relatives or were taken by soldiers. She will gladly lend the boat and help load it on a cart (moving it to the river needs the wanderers, Xu or Magistrate Fan).

Autumn 秋筠 eavesdrops throughout. What happens depends on whether the party mentions "the scar-faced woman":

  • Not mentioned: Spot Hidden / Listen notices someone at the window. Followed, a veiled young woman comes forward and apologises: she is Autumn, lodging here; her husband is across the river in Southbright; she came to visit kin, was abused and cut across the face, tried to drown herself and failed; Mistress Wang took her in. She will not show her face. Spot Hidden: thick calluses on her fingers, hard forearms ("rough work"). She begs to be taken across to her husband. She says she is good at disguise (fixed 70): while she lives, the party may ask her help once a day before acting, free. Tearing the veil off: opposed DEX vs 70, win by a level: a face crossed with scars. Hard Spot Hidden: some cuts are too neat, of different ages; critical: under them, the tattooed characters of a condemned prisoner. Accusing her of poisoning Ling Daiqiu starts the fight.
  • Mentioned: Spot Hidden sees the window open a crack and a white figure flash onto the roof; Listen hears light steps. DEX to catch her (bonus die if the first roll succeeded), then combat. Badly hurt, she shows the Undying form: first sight SAN 1/1D10 (1/1D4 if the party has already seen a Servant).

Autumn (human): STR 60 DEX 70 POW 60 CON 65 APP 70 SIZ 60 INT 65 · HP 12 · Sword 70, Dodge 65, Jump 65, Disguise 70. A famous outlaw of the Jinghu country with "a thousand faces"; caught by Fan and sacrificed; still a thief as an Undying. She stole the Ling needles and cast Green Rot 绿腐 on Ling Daiqiu. When she dies the green mould on Ling Daiqiu vanishes and he recovers. Until exposed she genuinely helps the party.

Autumn's room (after the fight Mistress Wang goes to look): incense, good-smelling, but Listen catches the same damp rot under it. Neat bed; under the vase two pages (handout "Green Rot"): the spell Green Rot 绿腐: chant, give the victim a fresh green leaf; the organs rot for seven days until the body is a heap of green mould; the only cure is to kill the caster. Reading it: SAN 1/1D4.

Wang Wu's Restaurant 王五分茶

The biggest eating-house in town (a 分茶). Shut on the 12th: last night the watchman accused them of hiding a thief; he and the owner fought and broke tables. From the 13th the waiters seat you warmly: beef noodles, braised duck tongues, all the local dishes. Eating here costs no round.

The "thief" is Chen Xunzhong 陈寻忠, Liu's standard-bearer, now an Undying Servant sheltered by Wang Wu; he stole medicine from HO2's pharmacy and Nameless Fang chased him here. Toghan 脱欢 eats here every noon in the best upstairs room (two guards at the door who taste everything first): the chance for HO2's revenge ("Blood debt", below).

Table talk: Wang Wu 王五条 is kind, gives rice gruel to the poor, caught a thief and let him go with money. Toghan comes daily at noon, second floor, best room; his two Tartars look down their noses and taste every dish.

Wang Wu (found any time after the poisoned meal) apologises for it and tells what he knows: Fan "loved the people, but nothing comes without cost" — then the whole plan: the rite, the sacrificed prisoners, the flotilla, the thing in the river. Chen: "a man I found at the riverbank with nowhere to go". The banquet: "the men left on the ships are old men and Song turncoats; General Toghan ordered us to bring them wine and meat on the night of the 17th." The raid: after a pause he agrees to let the party, the wanderers and the fishermen go in disguised as his delivery crew. (If HO2 poisons Toghan here first, Wang Wu shuts the shop and will not open this door; he asks to cross the river with the party.)

"Is this food poisoned?" Liu goes grey over his noodles and vomits blood, then is fine in a moment. Medicine: his pulse is far too steady for a living man; he is evasive. Tasting the food, Pharmacy / Medicine: a numb tongue; fresh pokeweed 商陆, harmless in small doses, bleeds the stomach in large ones, worse with wine. Spot Hidden: someone is watching (do not say who). After the meal Chen, dressed as a waiter, kneels weeping before Liu and HO3 and asks to meet them alone at midnight at the Street Crossing (→ Optional: "Rashomon alley"). Liu, overjoyed to see a comrade alive, waves the poisoning away as "drank too fast" and tries to keep HO3 out of what follows.

Blood debt: killing Toghan 不共戴天

If Wang Wu once owed HO2's family (famine relief in HO2's backstory; a low-morals HO2 may have none), he helps with the poisoning, the disguise and the way in; otherwise everything is done behind his back and discovery means arrest as thieves. Waiter disguise needs no roll; a successful Disguise avoids notice at close quarters. Chen will cooperate.

  • Kitchen: three cooks, two helpers, runners. The ready dishes stand apart; a PC can carry them up or let others.
  • Second floor, third room: an eight-immortals table, a silver incense burner, a screen inside the door, a decorative wardrobe (Stealth to hide in). Poison can go in the burner beforehand.
  • Toghan inside with two guards; two more at the door. Any noise brings the door guards. Only Toghan and the two door guards eat; guards still standing will try to save the poisoned, so they must be dealt with.
  • 牵机药 (bitter, strong scent, mask with strong wine or tea; 15–30 min) · 十香软经散 (colourless, instant; must be added to the wine in the room: Sleight of Hand under Mongol eyes).
  • Afterwards Wang Wu closes the shop in terror and asks to cross the river with the party. The warship raid can no longer start from here.

Toghan: STR 75 DEX 60 POW 50 CON 70 APP 55 SIZ 80 INT 50 · HP 15 DB +1D4 · Brawl/Sabre 75, Dodge 70, Spot 60. Bad Chinese, violent, moody; killed HO2's father; despises Duan.

The pharmacy (HO2's house) 药铺

Shut, two clerks busy inside. This branch is grasping: sky-high prices, clerks who size up a customer's purse. The manager fawns on the young master/mistress: HO2 may use staff, stock and cash freely. He produces two old recipes found in the storeroom (handout "Two poisons"): 牵机药 Bowstring (from ripe strychnine seeds; bitter, peculiar scent; stiffness after 15 min, the body arched like a bow after 30, grinning spasm, fully conscious, death by suffocation in about an hour) and 十香软经散 Ten-Scent Powder (ten spices with datura and 软骨草; white, odourless, tasteless; instant collapse of the limbs, martial skill gone after some days). Making either: Hard Medicine, once a day.

"A plea for medicine" (first visit): a girl in red with a long and a short curved sabre is arguing over prices: Ling Xuchun 凌序春. Her brother Ling Daiqiu 凌代秋 is dying of a strange poison and this is the only pharmacy with stock. What poison: Rainmaster's Ink 雨师墨, they say — "雨师墨黑，刀饮即腐；天若垂泪，骨露生蛆". Why: their family heirloom, embroidery needles thin as ox-hair and hard as iron, the perfect Acupoint tool, coveted by every master. They sheltered a woman; three days ago she stabbed her brother and ran with the needles; the blade was inked. The killer: Autumn, slender, a face crossed with scars; her brother found her by the river and took her for an orphan. Her brother: open-handed, nicknamed "排空击浪穿云翻天龙", the man every fisherman on the Han follows; if you need the fishermen, he can ask them, if he lives. The herbs she lists are all damp-dispelling: the neighbour doctor's recipe only eases the attacks. Leave word for her at the Wineshop. Cure him and she is yours for life; avenge him and the needles are yours.

Visiting Ling Daiqiu: a plain house in a lane on the river side of Front Street; fishermen call. He lies grey, breathing shallow, stinking of damp rot, the wound on chest and belly festering and not healing. Spot Hidden: fresh patches of mould around the wound, spreading; in his palm a fresh green leaf. Cured (by killing Autumn), his word brings the fishermen into the raid.

Ling Xuchun: HP 12, Sabre 70, Dodge 70, Climb 60, Swim 60. Ling Daiqiu: HP 13, Swim 75, Boat 70.

The Teahouse 茶楼

Three floors; private rooms above, a wide hall below with a storyteller's dais and, behind a screen on the right, the tea master's table where a thin white-browed old man sits. Song and Mongol customers mixed; nobody looks at the party. The storyteller is mid-tale: the Liangshan outlaws rescuing Song Jiang from the execution ground at Jiangzhou 江州劫法场 (plant it: the rescue of Niu will be exactly this).

Clues from customers, waiter, Listen: Niu shot Ashu's nephew dead among ten thousand men; he has a God-Arm Bow that shoots four hundred paces, "unless the Mongols have it now". The waiter recommends the tea master Song Zeyi 宋择一, "瓯面弄泉", whose tea-paintings even the emperor praised, "and Commander Fan thought the world of him".

Song Zeyi: a five-foot tea table full of cups; a short goatee; smiles; asks what picture you would like in your foam (flowers and birds: "you care nothing for office"; coins: "the wealth of the world"; characters: he tells their story). He pours and whisks with perfect ease.

"Tartar insolence": three Mongol soldiers at the next table laugh loud, insult the Song and the dead Commander Fan, kick the waiter over for weak tea, and shove the tea master's customers (the party included) aside to demand his tea. A scholar, Zhou Wentong 周文通, protests and is knocked down. Choices:

  • Soft: smooth it over (a woman's voice helps), bribe, or talk them down: a bonus die to any Sleight of Hand on them now. Ends with "The Mongols' general" below.
  • Hard: the soldiers draw. Song throws each PC a cup of tea with a picture — HO1 a red sun over crags, HO2 a willow bridge in wind, HO3 a dream of yellow millet — drink for a bonus die in the fight; then he stands on the screen and asks the party to settle it. Before each exchange he tosses another cup: DEX to catch, one bonus die each. Three soldiers (HP 12, Brawl 40, Dodge 40, armour 2); the house closes its doors and the patrols are not alerted for a while. Win and the owner cleans up; the general does not appear.
  • Watch: Song answers back, the soldiers wreck the place. Step in at any point for a fight. Never step in and Song gives no wineshop address and turns cold.

Song afterwards: the river's strangeness is "just weather" (open Psychology: he is hiding something). Fan was a good official who did everything himself; Song "helped him catch thieves" and knows nothing of what became of them or the condemned (opposed Psychology: hiding it). Boats: Prefect Xu's household keeps painted barges and fishing skiffs, "but the man guards his skin above all". Doctor Yue: he knows the "Hollow Physician" blackmailed Xu and disapproves — a wanderer should not break the law even for the poor. If the party helped, he gives the Wineshop's address: where the town's wanderers meet; going there costs no round.

Song Zeyi: HP 11, Throw 70, Jump 70. He helped Fan gather the sacrifices and hides it; he takes no part in anything to do with Gla'aki.

"The Mongols' general": a young Chinese general on horseback, Duan Driftwood 段游衍, passes the door, scolds the soldiers for brawling in town and wasting time, bows to the tea master and the party with perfect manners, looks twice at HO1 if present, and rides on.

The Coffin Shop by day 棺材铺

Shop front, courtyard behind; millet gruel, flat bread, pickles. Finished coffins with lids off drying their lacquer; Spot Hidden: hidden compartments in the walls. Winding Stream 曲流 works here by day: there are many dead in wartime; she made Commander Fan's coffin; people put the dead's belongings in the compartments against thieves and rot, "and young Master Fan asked for one too".

Evening of the 12th: Doctor Yue 越南柯 is chatting with her when the party returns (see the Session 0 runbook, Extended Day One). Boats: Xu's two unsent letters (handouts). Poison: "the local gazetteer might record it". Scar-faced woman: "either misfortune or a condemned convict". Fan: "far-sighted, devoted — executed a man for stealing a few taels of lamp oil".

The Undying family's house 某处民宅

Address from the gaol (the bun) or the burning house. A cold front hall, door shut. A pale young girl answers: mother and she have the fever. Told of her aunt's family in the fire she goes weak at the knees and falls, carefully, against Liu. She asks Liu in to carry firewood; HO2, a doctor, may come too. She and her brother are Undying; without Liu present she admits no one.

Neighbours (for those outside): the father died early; the son was sentenced to death the other day; the widow and daughter went to the river to make offerings and came back with "the fever"; the girl took things to kin near the Back Street guildhall a few nights ago; a tall man in white climbs their back wall at night. Spot Hidden at the back wall: bricks worn by frequent climbing; damp rot on the air from the yard.

  • By day: Liu, walking to the yard to chop wood, is suddenly "sunstruck" and sits silent drinking water; the girl says mother is asleep and asks them to leave, crying "they bully a widow and orphan" at any push. Outside, Liu speaks of the stench and a bad feeling and proposes coming back at night.
  • By night: Liu goes to the yard; the girl locks HO2 in an empty room (STR / Locksmith to get out) and HO2 arrives to find her attacking Liu.
  • The night raid 夜闯民宅 (night only; by day the neighbours beat "burglars" to death): over the back wall, the stink of the yard; Spot Hidden: the trough glows faint green, thick and foul, a bundle of clothes, two silver ornaments and a pair of embroidered shoes soaking in it (SAN 1/1D3). The girl and a tall white-clad man with tattooed cheeks appear on the porch and change: bones twisting, limbs drawn out into spines, skin rotting, nails long. First sight SAN 1/1D10 (1/1D4 if seen before). Combat; Liu is their first target.

Afterwards the bodies keep the monster shape: a healed wound on the spine, red web-lines over the back. Medicine: something sharp was driven in violently; the spine is altered and brittle; a thin point would snap it. Then a boy with a copper mallet and gong and a long cloth-wrapped bundle is crouching on the wall: Nameless Fang 方未名, the night watchman. He asks, examines the bodies, and says he must tell Niu. Told Niu is in the gaol, he asks for help and names the Wineshop for tomorrow.

The Wineshop (hidden; no round) 酒肆

In a lane off Front Street; address from the tea master or Ling Xuchun. Small, old, worn tables, two rows of great black-glazed wine jars under red cloth. The owner Du Guanshan 杜观山 greets you warmly and remarks that HO3 "is not really one of us". Regulars: Huaide the "Pagoda Arhat" 宝塔罗汉怀德和尚 and Nameless Fang.

The monk: "the great master from our temple — Iron Shirt and Golden Bell, try your acupoints on him, it's like pressing cotton! He's been here half a month and the temple dust must be a yard deep." Drinks or meditates at the wall. Each day he challenges one person to drink: three CON successes in a row win his golden kasaya 金袈裟 (armour 2, immune to fire). Fail and try again tomorrow. Tell him about the locked side hall or the footprints at the temple and he comes to the Temple fight.

Nameless Fang: "Niu sent him to me to feed. He beats the watches all night, sleeps badly, can't talk to people, but he's pure gold; Niu thinks the world of him. Keeps saying he must give back what he carries on his back." If the party met him at the Undying house, he tells them he went to find Niu that night and was told he was in the gaol awaiting execution; he rolls up his sleeve to show a bruised arm, and asks them to rescue Niu. (Ask around the gaol: last night a watchman killed four guards with a copper mallet.)

Du: HP 13, Blade 65, Dodge 60. Monk Huaide: use Du's numbers plus armour 2 and the kasaya. Nameless Fang: STR 70 DEX 70 POW 70 · HP 11 DB +1D4 · Mallet 75, Dodge 70, Climb 70, Spot 60. He carries the God-Arm Bow wrapped in cloth and does not know what it is.

Planning the rescue 救援牛富: the gaol is hard in and out; the condemned must pass along Front Street to the Street Crossing: "Like Jiangzhou! The street is lined with teahouse galleries and painted gate-towers — ambush from four sides like Chao Gai and Li Kui. Hands enough: Fang, Mistress Qu, the Jiang brothers, the Ling girl, Master Song from the teahouse, and me." (Only NPCs the party has actually met.) The wanderers' skills: the Jiangs know every lane and swim like fish; "nobody in Fencewall dares cross the Ling girl"; Mistress Qu is stronger than she looks, "they say she held her husband under in the well"; Song is slippery as a loach. Du draws Front Street with a tea-wet finger: stalls, and the painted gate-towers 彩楼 of silk and timber over shop doors, flimsy and ornate. The plan needs three parts: stopping the carts (who, how: topple a gate-tower, shoot the cart horses), finding Niu (three carts; only Fang knows his face, so only he can scout ahead and signal), getting away (route, who covers). Du fixes the meeting for noon-and-three-quarters on the 15th at the Street Crossing.

Back Street 后街

The Guildhall 会馆

The merchants' hostel, now the Mongol billet. Duan 段游衍 lodges here for convenience with his guards and adjutant; a gleaming fur carpet outside his door marks it. In by the front door with a token and a plausible story, or Climb up the back to the first floor (fail: injury).

Duan's room: a jumble of Ashu's gifts — an old curio shelf, a glittering coral tree, a painted wool carpet, literati paintings; two swords and a bow on the rack; on the wide desk brush, ink and paper, a short note, a letter, and a full defence map of Fencewall and Southbright.

  • The letter (handout "The Hermit's letter"), strong hand, signed Chen Yangshan 陈阳山: "You urged me several times to leave Mount Crag… I am old and my pupil is among wolves; how could I go alone? If HO1 succeeds, the name will be in the histories; if not, I beg you for old friendship's sake to save a life. I enclose what remains of Red Pine as payment…"
  • The note (handout "Toghan's note"), curt, from one general to another: the Marshal feasts the army at the Magistracy; the assault follows next day. Wang Wu's restaurant will feed the men left on the warships — ten oxen, eight sheep, thirty each of chickens and ducks, fifteen jars of old wine — delivered by the restaurant's own people on the evening of the 17th. "Few men on the ships; be watchful, let no rogue slip in. General Duan, see to it." → most soldiers go to the feast; the ships are thinly held.
  • The map: both banks, garrisons, places of note; the Watchtower 塔楼 on the Fencewall side is marked separately: "Fine view. Boats in the river and troop movements on the Southbright bank all in sight."

The burning house 会馆附近的民宅

Passing along Back Street the party meets a house on fire: dry winter, piled firewood, the neighbours helpless. An old woman begs for help: her niece's family, five people, two children under ten, trapped; the father died in the war last year and the pension never came.

The fire is an accident; the family are kin of the Undying house on Front Street and were all turned by the girl. They fear fire and cannot flee it. Beams and roof falling, smoke, burning furniture: DEX to get in or 1D3. The five hide in wardrobes and under beds; STR to drag one out — into the firelight, where its skin melts, spines push through and the body collapses into dark green liquid with a damp stench: SAN 1/1D10. The fire drives everyone out. Neighbours: "the whole family gone, only the cousin on Front Street left to bury them — and that house has had the fever and not come out for days." Ask, and they give the Front Street address.

Seven Treasures jeweller 七宝行

Lavish, selling gems and curios; no custom; a manager and one assistant. Information is traded for a game of stone gambling 赌石: Luck decides the stone cut open — fail: serpentine or quartz; success: aventurine or goldstone; Hard: Nanyang jade or sugar jade; Extreme: bright-green jadeite or royal lapis; critical: imperial-green jadeite or tianhuang.

The manager knows all the gossip and the Grand Lake Stone 太湖石: "Commander Fan ordered it here: two zhang high, eighty-one holes, 'letting through the north wind and the sounds of heaven and earth' — and in the forty-sixth hole a piece of green jade had grown. A wonder of the age; offered to the emperor it would have bought a marquisate. But the Commander wanted it brought into Fencewall to pray for the people of both banks, so I obliged him."

The Street Crossing 街口

Where Front and Back Street meet; you pass it going between them. Inns, tea stalls, and the execution ground: beheadings at noon-and-three-quarters, bodies hung until midnight.

12 January, noon: the Hermit 一月十二日

A crowd, a strange heavy mood. Today's body is a white-haired old man with one arm, a spear through his throat holding him in the air: the Hermit of Mount Crag 山阳道人. His face is calm, as if he had long expected this. HO1: SAN 1/1D3 if he mattered. From the crowd: Ashu went up Mount Crag to repay the pupil's sword-cut and took the seventy-year-old hermit, "and gave him a cut back — the hermit's famous Stillwater is three feet long, and Ashu's horse-cutting sabre took him in half". And: Ashu will behead the Song officials who refuse to submit, Niu among them, in a few days, "lucky young Master Fan surrendered so fast".

15 January, noon: the rescue of Niu 一月十五日 · 劫法场

Niu is brought from the gaol: 1D4+2 horsemen, 1D4+4 foot soldiers, three cage carts with draught horses. Secretly roll 1D3 for which cart holds Niu. Show the players the rules card "The rescue".

  • All friendly NPCs except Fang are commanded by the players and rolled by the GM. Players act, then soldiers; no DEX order. Soldiers attack whoever approaches the carts first. After five rounds reinforcements arrive; getting away with Niu is the win.
  • Stopping the road: topple a painted gate-tower at the right moment, or kill the cart horses.
  • From the galleries: anyone up high can attack any target with any ranged skill; a failure may hit a friend or a bystander.
  • Closing with horsemen or horses: combined DEX or Dodge + fighting skill; fail and a hoof does 2+1D3.
  • The carts: one round to reach, one round of STR or Locksmith to open. Three shackled prisoners in each beg to be taken; one PC/NPC carries one prisoner; Niu tells you to take the others first, but is too wasted to resist being carried.
  • Leaving: after five rounds the Mongols pour in. Horses, or into the lanes. Ranged PCs leave freely; melee PCs DEX, fail and a wanderer covers them and dies doing it. Mounted: bonus die; carrying a prisoner: penalty die.

Foot: HP 11, DEX 40, Blade 40, Dodge 40. Horse: HP 12, DEX 50, Blade 45, Dodge 40, armour 2.

Niu rescued: he tells all he knows and has Fang give the bow to the party ("I saw a young hero shoot like a god just now"); then he stays at the Wineshop and takes no further part. He knows Fan meant to "invite a god into the Han to stop the Mongols", not what it was: "he said he would take it to his grave". Before that Fan filled the death-cells with people whose crimes did not deserve it; a physician named Yue was nearly taken. The God-Arm Bow 神臂弓: 1D8+2, 400 paces; from the bank it reaches the middle of the river — the only bow in the scenario that does.

The Temple 寺庙

A small temple by the city wall, incense cold, untouched because Kublai honours the Buddha. One main hall and one side hall whose heavy door is shut, seemingly locked from inside. Spot Hidden in the dust: fresh footprints of many sizes.

Night at the temple 夜战山寺

Fires after the day's three rounds, on the night after Chen's invitation (Optional: "Rashomon alley"). If the party told the monk about the locked hall or the prints, he arrives during the fight.

  • The others: Liu proposes that he and HO3 keep Chen's appointment first "so as not to startle the snake". Let Nameless Fang's night round, or an Undying disguised as a passer-by, make the rest of the party suspect something.
  • HO3 and Liu: Chen leads them in by the back gate, asks HO3 to go quietly (make a secret roll for tension). Dead silence; the back hall door is open. Inside, Chen shuts the door and snuffs the candle. In the dark 1D4+2 Undying wait. Chen: "Set your mind at rest, my lord. We were fortunate: the Lady of the Han received us and ferried us over the sea of suffering to the land of the Buddha. General Liu should have come too — why will he never go with the Lady? She misses him so!" Liu's face changes; he tells HO3 he should have died with his men rather than live as neither man nor ghost. The old soldiers take their monster form, unarmed, attacking everyone including Liu at random. In the dark all HO3's and Liu's rolls are at −20 until the back door is opened and moonlight comes in. PCs outside arrive next round.

Afterwards Liu explains everything he knows: how the thing in the river turns people into its servants, and that he somehow escaped its control.

The Magistracy quarter 衙署一带

Commander Fan's residence 范天顺的宅邸

Plain and quiet; most servants dismissed. Magistrate Fan 范玉楼 accompanies visitors to pay respects in the mourning hall. An everlasting lamp burns at the study door.

The study: simple, elegant; a mahogany desk facing the window; calligraphy from friends; no weapon rack, two crammed bookcases. Spot Hidden: a nameless old book newly re-covered, pages very old, a traveller's record with several pages torn out; Library Use to skim (handout "The traveller's record"): "Beside Mount Qiao, in the Qiao river, lives a great fish called 何罗 He Luo: one head and ten bodies, like hundreds of fish entwined, writhing day and night… when I was exiled to Tanzhou, people near Lake Dongting had seen it: whenever it appears a great fog rises on the lake and no boat can pass." On the desk a Tang poem lies open (handout "The poem"): the poet carried off in a dream by a goddess and her attendants, waking on the shore of Lake Tai with voices still calling him.

The mourning hall: white banners, the three sacrifices on the altar, incense, a black-lacquered coffin in the centre. Winding Stream's hint about the compartment is the way in; the coffin can only be opened by sneaking in. STR to prise it: empty; Spot Hidden inside: the compartment, holding the torn pages (handout "The torn pages"): (1) "Who eats the flesh of the He Luo fish has his marrow washed and his spine drawn; a web of fine lines grows on his back. He needs no grain but cannot bear the sun, hiding by day and walking by night. All such learn the art called Green Rot… to undo it the person must be destroyed; there is no other way." (2) "The He Luo fish shuns light and heat and fears fire more than tigers, and so do those who eat it… it lies hidden on the river-bed and does not rise unless boats pass over…"

The assassination plan 刺杀计划

When the coffin's secret is found, Magistrate Fan appears at the hall door with a lantern and coldly accuses the party of insulting the dead. Accused of harming the people, he says plainly that it is this guest in the river that holds off the Mongol cavalry and shields the Song; the people of Fencewall have not had to live as slaves. Liu rages about his drowned army; Fan explains nothing. Guards are posted all round the house: no one leaves unless they accept his request. He means to use Ashu's desperation for a cure: kill Ashu.

  • The plan: HO1 and HO3 go in as HO2's assistants to treat the Marshal, and strike.
  • Guards: "the righteous have many helpers"; he will arrange a signal (the scholars).
  • Proof: Ashu is suspicious; the party must show they can cure the Ink — a cured patient, for instance. There is no cure; he suggests they fake one.
  • Weapons: none may be carried into Ashu's room; his guards are the pick of every tribe.
  • Help for the crossing: gunpowder, weapons. And: "when the commander dies the city will be in chaos — cross then."

Tell the players plainly: after the assassination they cannot move freely in Fencewall again (only the finale remains), so prepare everything first. If they refuse, hoofbeats outside: Fan, nervous, takes them for Mongols and lets the party out the back; outside, soldiers chase loose horses — Doctor Yue let them out of the Mongol lines to make the noise.

Prefect Xu's mansion 许德显的宅邸

Glittering, gate shut, nobody calling; servants sweep the forecourt. Xu 许德显, the fat prefect who runs the treasury, sits in his study with curios and a few maids. He can provide gunpowder, boats, and a way into the gaol for anyone without a token. Get to him by talking/bribing the sweepers (friendly bargaining) or over the back wall by Climb / Jump (then it is coercion).

Bribery, blackmail with his two letters, or fear ("when the court retakes the twin cities it will try the turncoats" — best from HO3 and Liu) all work: "Don't you know? His Majesty has moved two hundred thousand men from Huguang and the Zhe circuits to hold the rear. Southbright is a fortress and Lü Wenhuan 吕文焕 no fool; if it falls the armies close in and the Mongols are fish in a jar. Refuse us now and all your money will not keep your head on your neck."

Niu's house: Ashu's sickroom 牛富的宅邸 · 探怀出刃

Confiscated when Niu was gaoled; Ashu has taken it over. HO1 and HO3 disguised as HO2's assistants; Doctor Yue insists on coming as the experienced one (he can also supply fake-medicine materials). Facing the door an eight-immortals table under a painting of a general subduing barbarians; painted carpets, low tables, ox and sheep skulls, a horse-head fiddle; by the door a Mongol bow and three white-fletched arrows.

Ashu half-reclines on the bed: over eight feet, massive, the wounded arm bared, an eight-foot heavy sabre by his good hand. Kneeling beside him a Song girl who looks like Magistrate Fan (Fan Yuying 范玉莹, the Commander's daughter); behind the bed a Song physician. Two armoured Mongol guards inside and two outside, swords but no helmets, some acupoints (哑门 etc.) bare. Spot Hidden close up: the unwounded hand is less worn — not his sword hand.

Ashu knows of Ling Daiqiu's poisoning. To HO2 he is all kindness: condolences for the father, praise for the skill, rich promises. Suspicious, he allows no treatment until he holds a hostage: whoever HO2 names as kin, Doctor Yue steps forward as the elder brother and is led away. Then treatment may begin. His sabre stays by his left hand throughout; any sensitive move (a weapon, an acupoint touch) forces the fight. He talks all the while:

"My men came to the Central Plains and fell in love with its soft riches; none wants to go home. I only saw the south's charms myself when I came here. Look — that is Commander Fan's daughter. For all his loyalty, his daughter ends up holding a Mongol's broom. Doctor, tell me: what was it all for?"
"They say this place is thick with legends, the Lady of the Han above all. I used to wonder whether she was as lovely as they say. But since I came to Fencewall I have heard another version — that this goddess eats people. Is it true?"
  • The physician checks every medicine handed to Ashu; he can tell if it is tampered with, and says nothing.
  • Fan Yuying: Ashu makes whoever brings the medicine taste it first; she will not fight but blocks one blow for a PC and, when Ashu swings at HO2, slips her a dagger.
  • The scholars: during treatment, noise outside; a soldier reports scholars rioting at the gate, being dealt with; Ashu ignores it. This is Fan's signal: strike now and the outside guards do not come.

The fight: "the brave wins in a narrow pass" 狭路相逢勇者胜

Ashu snatches the sabre and cuts at the nearest (off hand: −20%). HO2 may Dodge; on a failure Fan Yuying takes the cut and passes HO2 the dagger. The guards draw; outside, steel rings; no help is coming. DEX order. The physician hides; Fan Yuying absorbs one hit for the party. After five rounds the deputy arrives and kills everyone — do not let it come to that.

  • Guards: HP 12, DB +1D4, STR 65, DEX 40, Dodge 40, Blade 40.
  • At this range a bow gets a bonus die and +1D4 damage; only the three white arrows are there. Grabbing the sabre is STR (1D8+DB). Taking bow or sabre costs a round.
  • Ashu to HO1: "Last time you were lucky. Back again, not afraid to die? I had that old man's head hung half a day longer for you — did you not see? You Song talk of virtue and use poisoned tricks. No matter. Let me see how much real skill you have." To HO2: "Your father did not know his place and neither do you. I wonder how much your sworn brother loves you — what will he think when he sees your head?" To HO3: "The draw is almost right; a long way from your Niu. Child, you have never killed a man, have you?"

Ashu at 0 HP ends it. Outside: chaos, scholars dead on the ground. Hold up his head and shout it, or slip away; the wanderers cover the escape and townsfolk help all the way out of the quarter.

Lockdown. The city goes under martial law; this is the night of the Watchtower. The Mongol attack on Southbright is postponed. Every move now needs Luck or Stealth; fail and a chase round begins (see the Cheat Sheet). Doctor Yue is held in another empty house of the Magistracy; the wanderers bring back a letter from him explaining the early summoning, and the news that he has burned himself to death — unless the party had him rescued first; either way he was ready to die. Magistrate Fan is beheaded on the spot and his head hung on the Watchtower.

The School and the Library 官学 · 藏书阁

Where the scholars lectured; unguarded, anyone may enter; a few scholars packing up. The library is inside. The scholar Kong Liyue 孔礼岳 takes the party for soldier-ruffians: "This is the house of Confucius and Mencius… you do not look like readers; the books here are a hundred years old, rare copies — what if rough hands damage them?" Zhou Wentong 周文通 rebukes him: he knows the town and can tell righteous men; Kong apologises.

Classics, histories, local gazetteers. Name the subject and Library Use (handouts "From the Library"):

  • Rainmaster's Ink: a local physician's notes: the wound festers and gives off a sick damp stench; the pulse clogs; the blood runs backward; deep poisoning spreads over the whole body; shallow poisoning festers for months or a year and then re-opens in every spell of rain. Idea: not quite Ling Daiqiu's case — nothing here about green mould.
  • The Lady of the Han: a book of local tales; one chapter is not the version you know: Zheng Jiaofu met the goddess, spoke rudely, asked for her pendant as a betrothal gift; she hid her anger, untied the pendant, and set a midnight tryst. He went and found no beauty, only a starving wolf five feet long, which ate him whole and left the pendant on the bank, unchewable. The place is called "the Lost Pendant Shoal".
  • Annotated Records of the Three Kingdoms: the local battle marked: Guan Yu attacked Fencewall when the Han flooded, drowned seven armies, shook the empire — then Sun Quan broke faith, Lü Meng took Jiangling, and Guan Yu was taken and killed at Linju.

Other scholars approach, praising the party's deeds (the teahouse) and cursing the Mongols and the court: "We too wish to serve the country, but we cannot lift or carry — hiding here, shameful!" They are Fan's kindling for the assassination day.

The Gaol 监牢

Heavily guarded; enter through Xu or with a token, and even then only the common cells — the Song officials who refused are deeper in. Damp mould, constant patrols, cold iron bars, most cells empty, a few haggard prisoners. From prisoners or guards: the empty cells held a batch of tattooed condemned men, some for petty theft, "taken out by Commander Fan to be beheaded a few days ago — not at the Street Crossing, and no bodies seen". And: Fan wanted to gaol the "Hollow Physician" too — "didn't he swindle Prefect Xu out of a fortune?"

The bun (optional): a thin boy in a cell begs: a condemned man gave him a flatbread and asked him, when released, to visit his sick mother; he cannot keep the promise — will they? Accept and get the Undying house's address.

Meeting Ashu: as the party leaves, Ashu and several Mongols come out from the depths with Magistrate Fan beside them. If HO3 is present Fan steers Ashu away from the party; Listen: Ashu smells of medicinal herbs. They talk loudly of Niu: "What a hard bone, this Niu!" "Stubborn, unbending, does not know that a wise bird chooses its tree. Hard bones or not, in a few days he goes to the Street Crossing — harder than our sabres?" Then Nameless Fang bursts in after Ashu has gone, grabbing people to ask where Niu is and about to fight the guards; stopped and calmed, he asks for help and names the Wineshop.

The riverbank 汉江沿岸

The Mongols garrison the high dock walls; few soldiers near the water itself. East dock: fishermen's huts. West dock: several Mongol warships moored, and desolation — a tall tower, a ruined pavilion, endless slender reeds.

East dock: the fishermen's huts 东码头 · 渔民棚屋

A straggle of huts along the dock edge. The fishermen are warm even in want: tea and salt fish. Boats: the Mongols forbid any private boat, and nobody could sail in this fog anyway. The warships: "the Mongols can't build ships and the Song craftsmen they dragged off are no masters — that keel, that deck, those gunwales — anyone who knew his trade could snap them." Fan: "took a crowd to the west dock the other day, sacrificing to some god, maybe." Strange things: people climbing out of the Han at night; whole families running to the bank; "a dragon — I saw it lift its head and stare at the Mongols on the shore!" Liu: "a fine young gentleman washed up a few nights ago, unhurt but for a bruised wound on his back crawling with red lines." A boatman: Ling Daiqiu, their undisputed leader.

The fishermen will not join the raid unless Ling Daiqiu asks them. With him, plan it here: on the feast night the ships are thinly held; the fishermen and local wanderers deal with the ships and their crews, the party keeps the shore guard busy. "Seven men on each ship, nearly thirty on the dock; half that on feast night. You gentlemen can't swim, so keep the shore men busy — drink and eat with them till they're stupid! We'll slip aboard and hole their hulls, then a fire to burn their southern dream!"

The Mongol warships: "Sink the ships, deny the crossing" 蒙古战船驻扎地 · 沉舟绝渡

Moored by the east dock, too well patrolled to approach — except on the night of the feast (17th), while Ashu lives. The party goes in with Wang Wu's delivery carts. 1D10+5 soldiers have deserted their posts to eat; almost all are Song turncoats; their centurion invites the party to join them.

Leave a few jars and some meat here; Liu takes the carts from ship to ship. The fishermen slip off the carts into the water to hole the hulls; the wanderers board to deal with the crews. Meanwhile the soldiers talk: home towns and families (the centurion has two small children), old trades (farmers, fishermen, pedlars), "we just followed our general; he surrendered, so we are Mongols now", and how the Mongols treat Song men like pigs and dogs.
